newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Izocam targets 10 pct increase in 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: Turk Izocam targets 10 pct increase in 1997 sales.

text.p: Turkey's leading insulation material producer Izocam Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S. hopes to raise its total sales by 10 percent in real terms next year to keep its 55 percent current market share, a senior company official said.

"We estimate a 10 percent market expansion in 1997 parallel to the construction sector and general economy and we will maintain our current slice," Hasan Eroktem, Assistant General Manager, told Reuters.
The company reported 2.84 trillion lira turnover in the first nine months of 1996, against 1.50 trillion in the same period of 1995.
"This result will lead us to meet the 3.7 trillion lira turnover target for 1996," he said.

Izocam had $49.5 million of total sales in 1993 which shrank to $36.5 million in the crisis year of 1994, before rebounding to $47.5 million in 1995. Eroktem said the 1996 figure would be around the 1995 result.

Izocam, an affiliate of the leading industrial Koc group, produces glass and stone based mineral wool, expanded and extruded polystren as a unique producer in the domestic insulation market for more than 25 years.
Izocam is the sole stone based mineral wool in the country with a 10,000 tonnes per year capacity.

It is one of the two producers of glass based insulation materials with a 20,000 tonnes per year capacity. Izotoprak of the Toprak group with a 10,000 tonnes annual capacity entered the market in April 1996.

Izocam started producing polystren in 1995 with two other companies, as the first domestic producers. Dow Chemical is the biggest polystren producer with 150,000 tonnes of annual capacity, followed by Izocam with 100,000 tonnes and BTM/Izmir with 35,000 tonnes.

The company would undertake an $8 million oven renovation and modernisation investment at its Tarsus and Gebze plants next year, Eroktem said, adding that production would be halted for one or two months during the renovations.
"We may also decide to expand capacities if the capacity utilisations force us to do, according to the rivals' market activities and export opportunities," he said.
The capacity utilisation rates in mineral wool and polystren were between 80 and 90 percent in 1995 and at around at the same level this year.
Eroktem said Izocam's export figure would be $10 million at the end of this year.
